newsitem.title: USA: Winfrey overtakes Spielberg as top-paid entertainer.
newsitem.headline: Winfrey overtakes Spielberg as top-paid entertainer.

text.p: Television talk show host Oprah Winfrey has recaptured the top spot on Forbes magazine's list of the world's highest paid entertainers, overtaking director Steven Spielberg.

The business publication says in its Sept. 23 issue that Winfrey earned some $171 million over the past two years, surpassing the $150 million earned by Spielberg, the director of "Schindler's List" and Jurassic Park," among other films.

Spielberg and Winfrey had ranked first and second, respectively, in last year's list. The annual rankings are based on income over two years in an attempt to gauge a person's "staying power" in the volatile entertainment industry, a magazine spokesman said.
In a real demonstration of "staying power," The Beatles, despite being long disbanded, remained in third position for the second consecutive year with income of $130 million in 1995 and 1996.

Pop star Michael Jackson ranked fourth with $90 million in income, followed by two other ageless rock groups -- the Rolling Stones ($77 million) and the Eagles ($75 million), who each slipped a notch from last year.
Action film star Arnold Schwarzenegger and magician David Copperfield ranked next with incomes of $74 million each, followed by movie comedian Jim Carrey with $63 million.

Author Michael Crichton, with royalties from the summer film hit "Twister" and top TV series "E.R." contributing to his $59 million in income, became the first writer to break into the top 10 in Forbes' list.
His $59 million income was matched by TV comedy star Jerry Seinfeld, who did not even make the top 40 last year.
